mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of tightening, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over the last six months indicates strong economic demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of GDP growth, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of falling unemployment, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in the last two months signals increased supply-side activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increased industrial production, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a broad-based increase in demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of simultaneous increases in housing starts and personal consumption, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 in the last month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong payroll growth, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% in the last two months signals a potential deflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of decreasing CPI, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP and a decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last six months signals a robust economic expansion, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase & UNRATE decrease > 0.3pp in 6 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of GDP growth and falling unemployment, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
